unit_title: Enforce the allowlist and manifest provenance in clean-runtime CI
standing_function: portable runtime execution from a clean clone
falsifiable_claim: The changed-path base resolves correctly for pull_request, push-with-before, new-branch push and unresolvable-base events, and an out-of-allowlist path fails the job.
local_verification: All four base-resolution branches were executed locally against this repository with the step script extracted from the workflow; each resolved to 552b12eacee637716451492a98980fb0da19ff3e and passed.
defect_found_and_fixed: The first implementation fell back to `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`, which pulled pre-existing base-branch content such as .cursor/environment.json into the diff and would have failed CI for commits this Wave never authored. Replaced with a PO-03 base-ref-first resolution order.

unit_title: Adversarial review of the path-scope guard and result-custody design
standing_function: independent evaluation, adversarial review and hidden-case generation
reviewer_independence_reason: No agent-dispatch tool, cursor-agent CLI or MCP create-agent capability is exposed to this worker, so a second-family reviewer could not be dispatched. See workstreams/po03/control/model-capability-register.json.
falsifiable_claim: The guard and manifest as first written admit at least one path by which a write outside the allowlist escapes detection.
measured_result: CONFIRMED. Two real defects reproduced in throwaway /tmp repositories: (1) `git diff --name-only` with default rename detection reports only the destination of a rename, so moving state/x.json into the allowlist deleted a governance file invisibly; (2) a tracked symlink under workstreams/po03/ caused manifest.py to hash content from outside the subtree, making the provenance claim false. Both fixed and covered by regression tests.
